evidence: No material accounting-integrity impairment identified in the reviewed 10-K, 10-Q, proxy or recent Form 4 filings.
Recent Form 4 tax-withholding dispositions are explicitly identified as such; the President's discretionary sale was under a disclosed 10b5-1 plan.
Growth is supported by $15.1 billion future contracted bookings and a $300 million undrawn revolver.
Axon used debt and ATM equity for acquisitions, investments and tax obligations, but this does not yet appear to be a structurally necessary funding model for core operations.
Shares outstanding increased from 76.62 million at year-end 2024 to 80.21 million at year-end 2025 and 81.24 million at June 30, 2026.
2026 SBC guidance is $590-$620 million; Employee XSP has a 4.5 million-share approved pool and CEO Performance Award includes 679,102 XSUs.
Axon sold approximately 0.2 million shares through its ATM in Q2 2026 and had about 1.0 million ATM shares remaining.
items.resolution_needed: Demonstrate that annual net dilution falls toward low-single digits or below as XSP/CEO award amortization matures and that per-share FCF growth outpaces dilution.

evidence: ARR grew 39%, NRR reached 126% and future contracted bookings grew 41%, indicating customer expansion rather than subsidy-driven growth.
Software & Services grew 36% with software-only gross margin above 80%.
No evidence of a structural collapse in product economics; Q2 GAAP operating margin improved and adjusted EBITDA grew more than 40%.
However, cash conversion is weak and acquisition intensity is high, so confidence is reduced.
NRR, ARR, bookings and ecosystem breadth indicate expanding rather than contracting customer relationships and switching costs.
Competition remains material in nearly every adjacent category.
At the latest confirmed close, AXON trades near 12.1x midpoint 2026 revenue and 47.6x guided adjusted EBITDA.
Reverse valuation implies roughly 18%-20% annual revenue growth for a decade under still-strong terminal economics.
items.resolution_needed: Either valuation must compress materially or evidence must support a credible path to sustained high-teens revenue growth with 20%+ owner-FCF margin and contained dilution.

evidence: U.S. revenue is concentrated at 81% of first-half 2026 revenue, but the company is diversified across TASER, sensors, platform solutions and software/services with no identified single-customer dependency.
Contracted backlog, recurring revenue and access to liquidity reduce bankruptcy risk.
Primary permanent-loss risk is valuation compression combined with dilution and acquisition misallocation rather than solvency.
